entity: AMA-Motorcycle Industry Council Combined Committee on Land Use
stance_basis: letter endorses ORV use and land access but demands scientific guidelines and fairer regulatory language as conditions
summary: The AMA-Motorcycle Industry Council Combined Committee on Land Use is mentioned within the American Motorcycle Association's comment letter as sharing the AMA's position that a comprehensive, science-based land classification system is necessary for fair ORV regulation. The Committee is actively working to hire a professional ecologist to develop such guidelines, and hopes the Bureau of Outdoor Recreation will collaborate on this effort. The entity supports ORV use on public lands but conditions that support on the establishment of objective scientific criteria rather than the draft's perceived negative and discriminatory tone.
complaint_summary: The AMA-MIC Combined Committee on Land Use endorses the Task Force's call for a scientific land classification system and announces it is hiring a professional ecologist to develop comprehensive guidelines for fair and equitable ORV land use, inviting the Bureau of Outdoor Recreation to collaborate.

statement.text:
This statement by the Task Force reflects very accurately the feeling of the American Motorcycle Association, and of the AMA-Motorcycle Industry Council Combined Committee on Land Use. This committee, composed of delegates from the AMA and the MIC, presently is reviewing resumes by professional ecologists. The group has resolved to hire one of these gentlemen for the purpose of establishing guidelines in a very comprehensive and clear textbook fashion. Through such a set of guidelines we hope to establish fair and equitable use of the land, knowing full well that some public land will be lost to the use of off-road recreational vehicles, yet with the feeling that our effort to cooperate will be returned by those with other interests.
Since the AMA and the MIC already have begun work towards such a set of guidelines, perhaps the Bureau of Outdoor Recreation or the Department of the Interior would be interested in working with us on such a study. I am sure that you will agree that such a study is necessary for proper implementation of Executive Order 11644.
